title: Single-Input Control of Multiple Fluid-Driven Elastic Actuators Via Interaction Between Bi-Stability and Viscosity
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the control problem of how to generate complex, coordinated state transitions in a chain of fluid-driven elastic chambers using only a single inlet flow input. The motivation comes from soft robotics and microfluidics, where controlling multiple actuators or valves usually requires many separate inputs and therefore greater system complexity.

The authors propose a method based on a serial chain of bi-stable elastic chambers connected by thin tubes. Their approach combines the chambers’ inherent bi-stability with viscous pressure lag in the tubes, allowing a single time-varying inlet flow rate to induce irreversible sequences of transitions among binary chamber states. The paper develops a mathematical model of the coupled fluid-structure dynamics, derives stability conditions for equilibria, and uses these results to plan state-transition sequences.

The work is demonstrated through numerical simulations and laboratory experiments with chains of 2, 3, and 5 latex chambers filled mainly with water-diluted glycerol. The results show that the system can realize prescribed transition sequences and multiple binary configurations with only one control input. The authors conclude that this mechanism could enable minimal-control soft actuators and suggests future extension to more complex soft robotic systems.
